Question: Michael walks at the rate of \(5\) feet per second on a long straight path. Trash pails are located every \(200\) feet along the path. A garbage truck travels at \(10\) feet per second in the same direction as Michael and stops for \(30\) seconds at each pail. As Michael passes a pail, he notices the truck ahead of him just leaving the next pail. How many times will Michael and the truck meet?
Solution:
Let \(t=0\) be the instant Michael observes the truck leaving the next pail. Define the truck's signed lead \(L\) as its position minus Michael's position, in feet. Initially \(L=200\); a meeting occurs exactly when \(L=0\).

The truck takes \(200/10=20\) seconds to reach the next pail, then stops for \(30\) seconds. During each drive, its lead increases by
\[
(10-5)\cdot20=100\text{ feet}.
\]
During each stop, Michael reduces the lead by \(5\cdot30=150\) feet. Thus each complete \(50\)-second cycle reduces the departure lead by \(50\) feet.

At departure times \(0,50,100,150,200,250,300,350\), the leads are respectively
\[
200,150,100,50,0,-50,-100,-150.
\]
Between consecutive departures the lead first increases and then decreases, so its minimum occurs at an endpoint. Therefore the first meeting is at \(t=200\).

From \(t=200\) to \(250\), the lead rises from \(0\) to \(100\) during the drive ending at \(220\). During the stop, Michael closes that \(100\)-foot gap in \(100/5=20\) seconds, giving a meeting at \(t=240\).

At \(t=250\), the truck is \(50\) feet behind. While driving it gains \(5\) feet per second, meeting Michael at \(t=260\). It reaches the next pail at \(270\), then \(50\) feet ahead, so Michael catches it \(10\) seconds later, at \(t=280\).

At \(t=300\), the truck is \(100\) feet behind. It closes this gap in \(20\) seconds, meeting Michael at \(t=320\), exactly when it arrives at a pail. This arrival and the start of the stop are one meeting.

At \(t=350\), its lead is \(-150\). Each later drive adds only \(100\) feet, and each later departure lead is still smaller, so no further meeting is possible. The five distinct meeting times are
\[
200,240,260,280,320.
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{5}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
